finding: Full bundle (shared chunks + index) totals ~295 KB gzip, which is 5.8x over the 50 KB budget; the budget appears to be measured against externalized Lit only via the esbuild analysis script, but the Vite dist includes all 80+ component shared chunks and the budget tracking gap is never surfaced in CI.
recommendation: Clarify in CI whether the 50 KB full-bundle gate is enforced on the Vite dist output or only on the esbuild analysis script; if the former, the library is in critical violation. Document which artifact the budget applies to and add an automated size-limit check against dist/index.js + shared chunks.

finding: Vite shared chunk hx-date-picker-Bh8410Sf.js is 7,407 bytes gzip, exceeding its 8,192 byte budget by 785 bytes on top of base Lit overhead, and the ariaLabel for each calendar day cell calls date.toLocaleDateString() inline per render with no memoization — on a 6-week grid that is up to 42 format calls per render.
recommendation: Cache the long-form day ariaLabel string alongside other day cell data in _getDaysInGrid() so it is computed once per grid rebuild rather than once per render cycle; or memoize via a Map keyed on ISO date + locale.

finding: hx-select gzip size is 6,330 bytes against a 6,144 byte budget, making it 186 bytes over. The override was declared in bundle-budgets.json but the component still exceeds that raised limit, which means CI budget gate would fail.
recommendation: Audit the hx-select styles file for removable specificity layers; consider hoisting the FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS string to module scope (same pattern as hx-dialog) to reduce per-instance string allocation, and verify floating-ui positioning logic is not being inlined unexpectedly.

finding: hx-nav-item shared chunk is 5,757 bytes gzip, 637 bytes over the 5,120 byte standard budget with no override declared in bundle-budgets.json.
recommendation: Add a justified override to bundle-budgets.json or reduce the component — audit hx-nav-item for inlined icon SVG markup or redundant CSS that can be extracted to CSS custom properties.

finding: hx-tree-item shared chunk is 5,819 bytes gzip, 699 bytes over the 5,120 byte standard budget with no override declared.
recommendation: Profile hx-tree-item for inlined SVG icons or redundant toggle/expand logic that could be moved to shared utilities; add a justified budget override if reduction is not feasible.

finding: hx-time-picker chunk is 5,775 bytes gzip, 655 bytes over standard budget; it does have a 6,144 override in bundle-budgets.json but the chunk gzip is measured under 6,144, so this is a near-limit warning.
recommendation: Monitor closely — the current size is within its override budget but only 369 bytes of headroom remains. Any new feature will bust the budget. Identify the largest CSS section via the bundle analysis script before adding further functionality.

finding: hx-form chunk is 5,753 bytes gzip (633 bytes over 5,120) with no override declared; hx-form uses an AdoptedStylesheetsController and inlines a large scoped CSS block (helixFormScopedCss) that is likely a significant portion of this cost.
recommendation: Declare a justified override in bundle-budgets.json or extract the scoped CSS into a shareable stylesheet that can be deduplicated across builds; evaluate whether the AdoptedStylesheetsController itself adds unnecessary overhead for a single-use component.

finding: hx-file-upload is 5,688 bytes gzip, 568 bytes over the standard budget; bundle-budgets.json grants a 6,144 override (so within its raised limit), but the component recently added a11y fixes that pushed it up from its 4.64 KB baseline.
recommendation: Confirm CI gates enforce the 6,144 override. If the component grows further with PHI or audit features, revisit whether file-list rendering could be lazy-loaded only after the first file drop rather than being included in initial parse.

finding: hx-carousel-item is 5,211 bytes gzip, 91 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget. The component itself is trivially simple (single slot, one property, minimal render), which suggests the styles file contains significant CSS or the document-token-adoption import is adding unshared overhead.
recommendation: Verify whether document-token-adoption is being included per-component chunk at the Vite level; if so, confirm it is always deduplicated into the shared chunk. 91 bytes over budget is very marginal and may vanish with minifier tuning.

finding: hx-data-table chunk is 5,241 bytes gzip, 121 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget despite extending LitElement directly rather than HelixElement, suggesting the JSON converter for the columns property and the large CSS block are the primary contributors.
recommendation: Add a justified override to bundle-budgets.json and document that the JSON column converter adds ~300 bytes; alternatively extract the converter to a shared utility that can be tree-shaken by consumers who pass typed arrays rather than JSON strings.

finding: hx-drawer chunk is 5,190 bytes gzip, 70 bytes over the 5,120 standard budget with no override; body-scroll-lock utility is a shared chunk but FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS is duplicated as module-scope constants in both hx-dialog and hx-drawer.
recommendation: The 70-byte overage is very marginal. Verify FOCUSABLE_SELECTORS is deduplicated by Vite's chunking strategy or extract it to a shared focusable-selectors utility module. Declare a budget override if reduction is not possible.

finding: hx-number-input chunk is 5,313 bytes gzip, 193 bytes over the standard budget; bundle-budgets.json grants a 6,144 override so this is within its limit. Long-press repeat key logic contributes complexity.
recommendation: Monitor headroom — 831 bytes remain before the override is breached. Document that the long-press timer and ElementInternals form association are the primary overhead drivers.

finding: sideEffects in package.json includes './dist/components/*/index.js' and './src/components/*/index.ts' as side-effectful, which means any bundler importing a single component from the barrel export will skip tree-shaking for all component index files; combined with the top-level barrel import in src/index.ts executing document-token-adoption.js at import time, the side-effect surface is wider than necessary.
recommendation: Narrow sideEffects to only './dist/utilities/document-token-adoption.js' and '**/*.css'. Component index files that only re-export named exports are pure and should not be listed as side-effectful.

finding: src/index.ts unconditionally executes import './utilities/document-token-adoption.js' at module evaluation time (not in a function), meaning any consumer who imports even a single named export from '@helixui/library' will trigger document.adoptedStyleSheets mutation as a side effect — even in SSR or test environments.
recommendation: The ensureDocumentTokens() function already has a SSR guard, but the bare import still causes the module to evaluate and attempt to read the Symbol.for key; wrap the auto-invocation with a typeof document guard or move auto-invocation to a separate side-effect-only entry point rather than the primary barrel.

finding: Each component individually re-imports document-token-adoption.js (100 files, 100 occurrences confirmed), resulting in 100 side-effectful import statements spread across the codebase. While Vite deduplicates this into a single shared chunk, esbuild-based consumer builds must also detect and deduplicate it.
recommendation: Since tokens are now adopted at the document level, the per-component import is redundant for any consumer that also imports the library barrel. Document this as intentional defensive coding and confirm the CI tree-shaking test verifies deduplication works correctly.

finding: preserveModules is not set in vite.config.ts; instead, code-splitting produces named shared chunks per component. While functional, this means consumers cannot reliably import a single component at a deterministic path without going through the per-component entry points.
recommendation: The per-component entry points in the exports map do provide deterministic paths. This is acceptable but should be explicitly documented as the canonical tree-shaking import path; the barrel import is only suitable for bundler-managed tree-shaking.

finding: 80 component files extend LitElement directly (bypassing HelixElement) while the remaining ~20 extend HelixElement. This inconsistency is not a tree-shaking issue per se but creates branching in the shared helix-element chunk that cannot be removed by tree-shaking even for components that only need LitElement.
recommendation: For purely presentational components with no form association (e.g. hx-carousel-item, hx-visually-hidden, hx-divider), extending LitElement directly is the correct and lighter choice. Document the decision rule: HelixElement only when form association or ElementInternals are required.

finding: _hueColor() and _previewColor() are plain private methods called directly in render() and _renderGrid()/_renderHueSlider()/_renderOpacitySlider() — each full re-render recomputes HSV-to-RGB conversion (hsvToRgb) and string formatting. During pointer drag events, this fires on every pointermove dispatching requestUpdate(), meaning color math runs at pointer-move frequency.
recommendation: Memoize _hueColor() and _previewColor() results as private instance fields computed only inside willUpdate() when _hsv changes; this avoids redundant computation during the render phase itself and reduces garbage pressure on frequently-updated strings.

finding: requestUpdate() is explicitly called inside _updateGridFromPointer(), _updateHueFromPointer(), and _updateOpacityFromPointer() after modifying _hsv (which is a @state), resulting in double-scheduling: assigning to a @state already schedules an update, and the additional requestUpdate() call is redundant.
recommendation: Remove the three explicit requestUpdate() calls from the drag handlers; the @state assignment on this._hsv is sufficient to schedule a Lit microtask update. The double scheduling currently causes no visible bug but wastes a scheduler round-trip on every pointermove.

finding: hx-date-picker uses updated() rather than willUpdate() to react to value and _isOpen changes, which means setFormValue, _updateValidity, and event listener attachment all run after the DOM has been updated and painted, adding a synchronous post-paint work unit.
recommendation: Move the setFormValue and _updateValidity calls from updated() to willUpdate(), which runs before the render and avoids an extra microtask. Only DOM-dependent side effects (focus management, event listeners that need the rendered calendar) legitimately belong in updated().

finding: _getDaysInGrid() is called directly in render() with no memoization. It allocates up to 42 Date objects per render plus the cells array. On every _focusedDay change (which is @state), the full grid is reconstructed.
recommendation: Move grid computation to willUpdate() and cache the result in a private field, invalidating only when _viewYear, _viewMonth, or value changes. This avoids reallocating 42 Date objects on every focus change.

finding: _renderDayGrid() creates inline arrow function click handlers for each day button via @click=${() => { this._selectDay(date); }}, which allocates a new closure per day per render. With 42 cells rendered each time any @state changes (including _focusedDay), this creates up to 42 closures per focus keystroke.
recommendation: Use a single delegated click handler at the grid level that reads data-day from the event target and dispatches to _selectDay, eliminating per-cell closure allocation. This is the same pattern already used in similar list-rendering components.

finding: Across 50 components, updated() is used; of these, hx-date-picker and hx-dialog set @state fields inside updated() (e.g. _liveMessage, _viewYear, _viewMonth), which triggers a second render cycle synchronously. While the guard conditions prevent infinite loops, the double-render pattern wastes a microtask.
recommendation: Prefer willUpdate() for all state synchronization that does not require reading from the rendered DOM; reserve updated() only for side effects that need the new DOM (focus management, third-party library calls, ResizeObserver registration).

finding: hx-combobox uses repeat() with correct key functions for the option list, which is good. However, the debounce implementation for filtering is not visible in the first 80 lines reviewed; if filter operations run synchronously on every keystroke without batching, long option lists will block the main thread.
recommendation: Verify that the filter step in hx-combobox uses a debounce or schedules filtering via requestAnimationFrame; if filtering is synchronous with large option sets, add a debounce with a 100-150ms delay matching the INP budget.

finding: hx-data-table uses repeat() for row rendering which is correct. However it extends LitElement directly rather than HelixElement and does not guard JSON parsing of the columns attribute behind willUpdate(); the converter runs on every attribute mutation regardless of whether columns actually changed.
recommendation: Move JSON parsing validation into willUpdate() behind a changedProperties.has('columns') guard to avoid redundant parse operations when other properties change.

finding: hx-nav uses repeat() with index as key rather than a stable item identifier (_item, i) => i, which means when items array is reordered, Lit cannot reuse DOM nodes — it treats every reordering as a full replacement.
recommendation: Use a stable key from the item itself (e.g. item.href or item.label) instead of the array index. Index-based keys are equivalent to no keys in terms of DOM reuse on reorder.

finding: guard() and cache() directives from lit/directives are not used anywhere in the component library (0 occurrences). For components with expensive sub-trees that rarely change — such as hx-color-picker's gradient grid SVG, hx-data-table's header row, and hx-date-picker's weekday header row — guard() would prevent unnecessary virtual DOM diffing.
recommendation: Add guard() around hx-date-picker's weekday headers (_renderWeekdayHeaders) which is locale-only dependent and never changes mid-session; add guard() around hx-color-picker's grid background when only the thumb position changes.

finding: hx-dialog calls querySelector('...') inside render() when deriving the trigger element for focus restoration: this.shadowRoot?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[part="trigger"]'). This pattern forces a DOM query on every render rather than using the @query decorator.
recommendation: Refactor the focus-target resolution to use a @query decorator or a cached private field populated in firstUpdated(); querySelector in render() is documented in the agent system prompt as an anti-pattern to avoid.

finding: The deprecated mergeTokenStyles() function remains exported in src/base/styles.ts with a @deprecated JSDoc tag but is still re-exported from src/index.ts, meaning tree-shakers that cannot eliminate re-exports will include it in every consumer build.
recommendation: Remove the mergeTokenStyles export from src/index.ts with a semver-appropriate deprecation timeline; the function's body is minimal but its presence in the public API prevents the associated module from being eliminated by bundlers.

finding: CSS custom property chains use three-tier var() nesting (primitive -> semantic -> component-level) across all component styles. While this is the correct design-token architecture, deep var() chains can cause recalculation cascades in browsers when a parent token changes, especially if the same token is read in many selectors.
recommendation: This pattern is architecturally correct. Ensure tokens are only read at the :host level via local private custom properties (--_bg: var(--hx-button-bg, var(--hx-color-primary-500))) and that inner selectors reference only the private alias, not the full chain — this minimizes style recalculation scope.

finding: hx-form uses Light DOM rendering (createRenderRoot returns this) and injects scoped CSS via AdoptedStylesheetsController, which writes to document.adoptedStyleSheets. The scoped CSS for a single form component competing with other document-level stylesheets increases selector specificity requirements and can cause layout recalculation when a form is first rendered.
recommendation: Audit helixFormScopedCss for any selectors that match broad document-level elements (e.g. input, label, select without component prefix) — these will affect all matching elements in the document, not just those inside hx-form. Scope all selectors to :is(hx-form *) or a unique class to prevent bleed.

finding: hx-color-picker's gradient grid uses styleMap() to set --_hue-color and --_thumb-x/--_thumb-y on inline styles during every drag event. This is correct (CSS custom properties on inline style trigger minimal recalc), but the --_preview-color is also computed in render() via _previewColor() and applied via styleMap, creating a pattern where three separate style computations run per render.
recommendation: Combine all dynamically-updated CSS custom properties into a single styleMap call on the host element or a single container, reducing the number of style attribute updates per render cycle from 3+ to 1.

finding: Zero production dependencies beyond Lit core and workspace tokens are present in the library's dependencies field — @floating-ui/dom is correctly listed as a peerDependency, preventing it from being bundled. This is excellent dependency hygiene.
recommendation: Maintain this constraint strictly. Any future utility (date formatting, color parsing beyond the internal color-utils.ts, validation) must remain internal or be gated as a peerDependency. The current zero-deps policy is a competitive advantage.

finding: color-utils.ts is an internal module implementing full HSV/RGB/HSL/HEX color math without pulling in any external color library — this is the correct approach for keeping bundle size within the 8KB override budget. The entire color math adds approximately 1-1.5KB gzip.
recommendation: No action needed. Document explicitly in bundle-budgets.json that the color-utils.ts is the intentional internal replacement for external color libraries like chroma.js or tinycolor2.

finding: No IntersectionObserver-based lazy registration patterns exist anywhere in the library codebase. Heavy components (hx-color-picker 6.97 KB, hx-date-picker 7.4 KB, hx-combobox 6.9 KB, hx-data-table, hx-form) are registered eagerly via @customElement decorator at import time — there is no mechanism for deferring their registration until first use.
recommendation: Provide documented lazy-loading examples in the Drupal integration docs showing IntersectionObserver-based dynamic import() for hx-color-picker, hx-date-picker, and hx-combobox. These three components alone account for ~21 KB gzip and are typically used on specific form pages rather than site-wide. No source changes required — documentation and Drupal behavior examples are the deliverable.

finding: The CDN build strategy documented in build-cdn.mjs produces a Strategy A (full bundle ~816 KB raw) that loads all 80+ components synchronously, which is the primary Drupal delivery mechanism. No lazy-loading documentation exists for the CDN path; all components load regardless of whether the current Drupal page uses any of them.
recommendation: Publish a Drupal-specific lazy-loading pattern using the Strategy B split bundle output (per-component CDN files) paired with IntersectionObserver or Drupal behaviors; add this to the Drupal integration docs. The split bundle output already exists in dist/cdn/components/.

finding: hx-dialog, hx-drawer, hx-color-picker, and hx-date-picker are modal/overlay components that are universally off-screen on page load — they are ideal IntersectionObserver candidates but all four are included in the CDN full bundle without any lazy-loading infrastructure.
recommendation: Add a documented withLazyRegistration() helper or a separate lazy entry point (e.g. @helixui/library/components/hx-dialog/lazy) that uses dynamic import() gated on IntersectionObserver intersection; this pattern would defer 4 of the 5 heaviest components until needed.

finding: hx-carousel and hx-carousel-item are typically used below-the-fold on content pages and would benefit from lazy registration, but the carousel-item chunk is already over budget (5,211 bytes) and both components are registered at import time with no deferred-import path.
recommendation: Document hx-carousel as a lazy-load candidate in the performance guide; provide an IntersectionObserver pattern specifically for carousel since images inside typically are the LCP candidate and delaying carousel JS registration can meaningfully improve LCP.

finding: The bundle-analysis.js script documents the IntersectionObserver lazy-loading pattern in its recommendations section (intersection-observer-lazy), but this is only visible in the audit JSON output — no equivalent documentation, code example, or Drupal behavior file is published for consumers.
recommendation: Surface the lazy-loading pattern from bundle-analysis.js recommendations into the public Astro Starlight docs and the Drupal CDN integration guide; add a concrete code example for hx-color-picker and hx-date-picker.

finding: hx-button uses classMap() and ifDefined() directives correctly. The loading state conditionally renders a spinner SVG using the nothing sentinel, which is the correct Lit pattern for conditional rendering.
recommendation: No action needed. hx-button is a well-optimized Lit component — @query is used for DOM references, willUpdate() handles property synchronization, and nothing is used for conditional sections.

finding: hx-select uses repeat() with (opt) => opt.value as the key function, which is correct. However the dropdown listbox is conditionally rendered on _open state — while correct for reducing DOM, this means every open/close cycle fully destroys and recreates the listbox DOM including ARIA attributes, which may cause flicker in screen readers.
recommendation: Consider using Lit's cache() directive or a CSS visibility pattern for the listbox to preserve ARIA live region state across open/close cycles; this trades a small constant DOM cost for improved AT continuity.

finding: hx-pagination uses repeat() for page number rendering with stable keys ('ellipsis-N' or 'page-N'), which correctly enables DOM reuse when paginating through large datasets.
recommendation: No action needed. Pagination render optimization is correct. Verify that the repeat key includes both page number and ellipsis type to prevent DOM identity confusion when ellipsis positions shift.

finding: hx-file-upload uses repeat() for file list rendering with (entry) => entry.file.name + entry.file.size as the key, which is a good approximation but could collide for files with identical names and sizes. More importantly, the progress state updates for individual files will cause repeat() to reconcile the entire list on every progress tick.
recommendation: Add a stable unique ID to each file entry at upload time (e.g. a monotonically incrementing index or crypto.randomUUID()) and use that as the repeat key; this eliminates any key collision risk and makes DOM reconciliation O(1) per file rather than O(n).

finding: hx-time-picker uses repeat() for time slot rendering with (slot) => slot.value as the key, and the slot list is only rendered when _open is true — this is good. However the slot list appears to be rebuilt on every open rather than being memoized, meaning potentially hundreds of time option objects are reallocated per open.
recommendation: Compute the time slots array once in connectedCallback() or the first time the picker opens and cache it; time slots are deterministic from the step property and do not need recomputation on each open unless step changes.

finding: The aria-delegation mixin (mixinDelegatesAria) used by hx-button intercepts all 40+ ARIA attributes via observedAttributes and re-dispatches them to the inner button element. This means every ARIA attribute set on the host element triggers attributeChangedCallback, a property access, and an attribute set on the inner element — three DOM operations instead of one.
recommendation: Profile whether the aria-delegation overhead is measurable for interactive components like hx-button used in high-frequency scenarios (data tables with hundreds of buttons). If overhead is measurable, consider limiting the intercepted attribute list to only those actually needed by each component rather than all 40+ ARIA attributes uniformly.

finding: hx-counter implements animated number counting, which by definition involves rapid @state updates driving re-renders at animation frame rate. The component calls requestUpdate() in the animation loop — it is unclear if this is guarded by willUpdate() to batch updates or if each increment triggers a full Lit update cycle.
recommendation: Verify the counter animation uses requestAnimationFrame and batches state updates; if _currentValue is a @state that is incremented per frame, consider using this.requestUpdate() only and updating a non-reactive private field directly, then triggering a single render at the end of each frame via requestAnimationFrame.

finding: Per-component entry points are correctly implemented via auto-discovery in vite.config.ts (discoverEntryPoints()), covering all hx-* component directories and exposing each as a named Rollup entry. The exports map in package.json correctly surfaces './components/*' paths.

Vite build uses minify: 'esbuild' which is the fastest and produces competitive output size. All Lit packages and @helixui/tokens and @floating-ui are correctly externalized via the external regex patterns, preventing any accidental bundling of the Lit runtime into component chunks.

Shared utilities (body-scroll-lock, id-counter, helix-element, document-token-adoption, aria-delegation, FormMixin) are correctly extracted into named shared chunks by Vite's code-splitting, preventing duplication across component chunks. The 14 shared chunks confirm effective deduplication.

devWarn utility correctly uses import.meta.env.DEV which is statically replaced at build time by Vite, meaning all devWarn calls are eliminated from production builds as dead code. This is the correct tree-shaking pattern for development-only utilities.

body-scroll-lock is implemented as a 58-line internal utility with a reference-counted stack pattern, avoiding any external lock library dependency. The module-level state (_lockCount, _savedOverflow) is correctly handled to prevent race conditions between multiple overlays.

hx-date-picker correctly memoizes Intl.DateTimeFormat instances (_weekdayFormatter, _monthFormatter, _cachedWeekdayNames) and rebuilds them only when locale changes via _ensureFormatters(). This is a good optimization for a component that renders 7 weekday headers and a month name on every calendar open.
recommendation: No action needed on the formatter memoization. Consider also memoizing the full-form day ariaLabel format (noted separately under render-performance) using the same locale-keyed pattern.

finding: @query decorator is consistently used across components for DOM element references (hx-color-picker, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-text-input all use @query), correctly avoiding querySelector calls in the render path.

hx-color-picker correctly caches bounding rect at pointerdown (_dragRect) rather than reading getBoundingClientRect() on every pointermove event. This is a significant render-performance optimization that avoids forced synchronous layout on every drag frame.

Shadow DOM encapsulation is used consistently across all components. The document-token-adoption adopted-stylesheet pattern correctly provides CSS custom property inheritance through Shadow DOM boundaries without per-component token redeclaration, which is the optimal architecture for a Lit component library.
